property_summary: After a successful initialize with valid product info, the product exposes exactly the given name, symbol, maintenance, makerLimit and fee parameters, and starts out not closed.
After a successful initialize, the product's stored maintenance and makerLimit parameters exactly equal the values passed in the ProductInfo, and it is not closed.
initialize is one-shot: a second call to initialize always reverts with the already-initialized error, for any valid product info.
After a successful initialize, a second initialize call with the same product info always reverts.
A second call to initialize always reverts even when the new ProductInfo differs from the one used in the first, successful initialization.
On a not-yet-initialized product, calling settle() must revert for every input, and afterwards no account has any maker/taker position and latestVersion() remains 0.
On a freshly deployed (uninitialized) Product, updateOracle must revert for any caller, since only a registered product owner may update the oracle.
On a freshly deployed, uninitialized product, updateClosed must revert for every input since only a registered product owner may call it.
On an uninitialized product, updateClosed always reverts and closed() remains false afterward.
On a freshly deployed uninitialized product, openTake always reverts (onlyProductOwner/settle path fails) and no position is created.
updateClosed on a freshly-deployed C always reverts for any caller that is not the product's coordinator owner (access control), for every input flag.
closeMakeFor always reverts for any caller that is neither the account itself nor the product owner, and leaves the account's position unchanged.

property_summary: closeMakeFor always reverts for any caller that is neither the account itself nor the product owner, and leaves the account's position unchanged.

On a fresh (uninitialized) product, positionAtVersion returns an empty Position (zero maker and taker) for every oracle version queried.
On a fresh (uninitialized) product, the maintenance requirement for any account is always zero (no position exists).
On a freshly deployed (uninitialized) product, any owner-protected parameter update like updateClosed must revert since the caller cannot be the coordinator owner.
On a freshly deployed Product, the utilization buffer is always zero, so max utilization equals one for any position regardless of inputs.

property_summary: updateFundingFee always reverts when the proposed funding fee exceeds 1e18 (one), for any caller, and the stored funding fee remains unchanged.
For any account with no positions ever opened, the product reports a zero maker/taker position and account latest version of zero.
closeMakeFor can only be invoked by the account itself or the product owner; any other caller's attempt reverts and leaves the account's position unchanged.

On a freshly deployed product whose controller is not initialized, every state-changing entry point (settle, updateMaintenance) must revert, and the maintenance parameter stays zero for any attempted value.
On a fresh (uninitialized) product, every attempted state change reverts, so the maintenance parameter remains zero for any attempted value.
On a freshly deployed (uninitialized) product, any attempted state change (updateFundingFee with any value) must revert, so the funding fee parameter remains zero for all inputs.
On a freshly deployed, uninitialized product, updateMakerFee always reverts and the maker fee parameter remains zero for any attempted value.
On a freshly deployed, uninitialized product, updateClosed always reverts and closed() remains false for any attempted value.

On an uninitialized-but-deployed Product, for every account the product is open, not paused-closed, not liquidating, and all position/pre-position/version/maintenance state reads are zero, guaranteeing positions only ever exist after real protocol actions.
closeMakeFor must revert unless the caller is the account itself or the controller owner, for any account and amount.
On a freshly deployed Product, openTakeFor reverts for every account and amount, and no taker position is opened for that account.
